# EMET — Gospel of Mary, Chapter 6
**Agent:** EMET (Literal/Transparent)
**Source:** P.Berol. 8502, Gospel of Mary, p. 9-10 | Coptic
**Chapter:** 6

---

**6:1** But they were grieved. They wept greatly, saying, "How shall we go to the Gentiles and preach the gospel of the Kingdom of the Son of Man? If they did not spare him, how will they spare us?"

**6:2** Then Mary stood up, greeted them all, and said to her brethren, "Do not weep and do not grieve nor be irresolute, for his grace will be entirely with you and will protect you.

**6:3** "But rather, let us praise his greatness, for he has prepared us and made us into men."

**6:4** When Mary said this, she turned their hearts to the Good, and they began to discuss the words of the [Savior].

---

*Translator's Note (EMET):* Verse 6:1 — "Gentiles" translates Coptic *ethnos* — EMET preserves the term as it stands rather than rendering "nations." Verse 6:3 — "made us into men" (*anthrōpos*) — EMET preserves the literal Coptic; this is theologically significant: Mary uses the Gnostic anthropological category of the perfected human. Not "mature persons" — the Coptic *andreia* (lit. "men/manly") is part of the text's Valentinian anthropology. Verse 6:4 — "the Good" retains capital-G Platonic resonance.
